body:
## Problem

No contributor guide exists at `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`, while the repository enforces a CI validation gate. The `contributing` command classes this as High.

## Evidence

`git ls-files` lists no CONTRIBUTING file at any of the three locations. .github/workflows/validate.yml runs pre-commit on pushes and pull requests to `main`. The validation commands and conventions are recorded only in CLAUDE.md, which is written for an agent.

## Impact

A human contributor has no stated setup, validation command, or pull-request process and learns the requirements from a failing CI run.

## Fix

Add `CONTRIBUTING.md` with sections generated from existing sources: intro from README.md, code style from .editorconfig and .yamllint.yaml, validation from `pre-commit run --all-files`, and pull-request process from validate.yml and .github/CODEOWNERS. Offered through the apply-fixes prompt.

## Resolution
Added CONTRIBUTING.md generated from .editorconfig, .yamllint.yaml, CLAUDE.md, validate.yml, CODEOWNERS, the main ruleset, git log, and LICENSE. Setup and issue-reporting sections omitted because the repository has no source for them.
title: CONTRIBUTING.md is absent in a repository with a CI gate

body:
## Problem

Class: model-as-security-control. Line 13 turns on Automatic Approvals for every repository that consumes this file, through its legacy alias. The config has no `reviews.auto_approvals` block, so `max_merge_risk` and `max_security_risk` are unset and `allow_author_approval` stays at its default of `true`. A PR author can therefore obtain CodeRabbit's approval by posting a comment.

## Evidence

coderabbit.yaml:13: `request_changes_workflow: true`

coderabbit.yaml:124-134: all four pre-merge checks use `mode: warning`. schema.v2.json on those modes: "`warning` posts a warning, and `error` requires resolution before merging. If the request-changes workflow is enabled, `error` can block the PR until the check passes."

docs.coderabbit.ai/pr-reviews/automatic-approvals: "CodeRabbit also reads `reviews.request_changes_workflow` and treats it as `reviews.auto_approvals.enabled`."; "CodeRabbit's approval counts toward your Git provider's required approvals."; "With Automatic Approvals turned on, both can also approve the pull request without a completed review of the latest commit and without passing Pre-Merge Checks."; "By default, pull request authors can use both commands on their own pull requests."

docs.coderabbit.ai/pr-reviews/approval-policies: "With a single required approval, an author's `@coderabbitai approve` comment can satisfy the requirement without a completed review of the latest commit or passing Pre-Merge Checks."

Schema, `max_merge_risk`: "merge risk is unrestricted only when no configuration source sets a limit."

Failing scenario: a consumer repository requires one approving review and has no code-owner rule. The PR author comments `@coderabbitai approve`. CodeRabbit approves without a completed review of the latest commit, and the approval satisfies the branch rule.

## Impact

On a consumer repository with that branch rule, a required review no longer proves anyone independent looked at the change. The exposure is bounded: an approval does not merge, so merging still needs write access or automation. This repository is not affected, because its `main` ruleset requires code-owner review. Consumer repositories' branch rules were not inspected. Docs state the Free plan does not approve and that Automatic Approvals needs the Essentials plan or above.

## Fix

Replace line 13 with the block below. This changes behavior, so it needs owner approval. If self-approval is intended for solo-maintained repositories, set `allow_author_approval: true` explicitly and keep the risk limit.

```yaml
  auto_approvals:
    enabled: true
    allow_author_approval: false
    max_merge_risk: low
```

## Resolution
reviews.auto_approvals now sets enabled: true, allow_author_approval: false, max_merge_risk: low. Validated against schema.v2.json.
title: Automatic approvals enabled with no risk limit and author self-approval allowed

body:
## Problem

The `.github/**` path instruction tells the reviewer, for every consuming repository, that actionlint is wrong about `${{ ... }}` in conditionals and about removing it. actionlint's `if-cond` rule reports a real defect in exactly that syntax.

## Evidence

coderabbit.yaml:63-66: "'actionlint' erroneously generates false positives when dealing with GitHub's `${{ ... }}` syntax in conditionals." and "'actionlint' erroneously generates incorrect solutions when suggesting the removal of valid `${{ ... }}` syntax."

Reproduced with actionlint 1.7.12 on a planted step using `if: ${{ false }} && github.ref == 'refs/heads/x'`:

`if: condition "${{ false }} && github.ref == 'refs/heads/x'" is always evaluated to true because extra characters are around ${{ }} [if-cond]`

coderabbit.yaml:191-192 enables actionlint, so the reviewer receives this tool output together with an instruction to discount it.

## Impact

A workflow step guarded by an always-true condition runs unconditionally, which matters for deploy and release steps. The instruction steers the reviewer away from the one tool reporting it, in every repository using this config.

## Fix

Delete lines 63-66. If a specific false positive exists, replace them with one line naming its actionlint rule ID and a minimal reproducing expression.

## Resolution
Removed both actionlint statements from the .github/** path instruction; a grep for "erroneously" finds nothing.
title: Shared .github prompt labels a real actionlint bug class as false positives

body:
## Problem

The path is `docs/*`, which matches only direct children of `docs/`. The instruction text describes "the `docs/` directory tree" and `docs/**.md`, so nested documentation does not receive it.

## Evidence

coderabbit.yaml:67: `- path: docs/*`; coderabbit.yaml:70: "Consider the files in the `docs/` directory tree the core/main/in-depth".

docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration/path-instructions: "Paths accept glob patterns. See the minimatch documentation for more information."

Tested with the minimatch bundled in npm:
- `docs/*` vs `docs/README.md`: true
- `docs/*` vs `docs/guide/intro.md`: false
- `docs/*` vs `docs/plans/x.md`: false

## Impact

Files such as `docs/guide/intro.md` get no grammar, clarity, or language guidance from this entry in any consuming repository. The markdownlint and LanguageTool integrations still run independently.

## Fix

Change line 67 to `- path: "docs/**"`. `docs/plans/x.md` will then match both this entry and `docs/plans/**`; CodeRabbit's docs do not state how overlapping entries combine, so check one nested file with `@coderabbitai configuration` or a test review after the change.

## Resolution
Path changed to "docs/**"; minimatch confirms it matches docs/guide/intro.md. Overlap with docs/plans/** remains undocumented by CodeRabbit.
title: docs/* path instruction misses the subdirectories its text covers

body:
## Problem

Most of the file repeats schema defaults, including 37 `enabled: true` tool entries. The explicit tool list does not determine which tools run, because tools left out are also enabled by default.

## Evidence

Comparing each set value with the `default` in schema.v2.json gives 97 equal to the default, 13 changed, and 1 with no schema entry (`timeout_ms`).

coderabbit.yaml:135-222 lists 38 tools, 37 with `enabled: true`. The configuration reference documents 59 tools. The 21 not listed include `trivy`, `zizmor`, `trufflehog`, and `osvScanner`; the reference gives those four `default: true` for `enabled`.

## Impact

The 13 settings that express a real decision are buried, and the tool list suggests a curated selection that does not exist. Repeated defaults also stay pinned if CodeRabbit changes a default, while unlisted settings follow it, so the file gives inconsistent protection against upstream changes.

## Fix

Delete every key whose value equals the schema default, keeping `tone_instructions`, `early_access`, `reviews.high_level_summary_in_walkthrough`, `reviews.auto_title_instructions`, `reviews.auto_apply_labels`, `reviews.auto_assign_reviewers`, `reviews.path_instructions`, the approvals setting, `reviews.auto_review.drafts`, and the four Jira and Linear `usage: disabled` keys. Effective behavior is unchanged as long as CodeRabbit's defaults stay as published on 2026-11-10.

## Resolution
Removed the 97 keys equal to their schema default; a leaf-by-leaf comparison with HEAD found no other removal. File reduced from 254 to 100 lines.
title: 97 of 111 scalar and list settings restate CodeRabbit defaults

body:
## Problem

Class: config-drift. README.md:9-10 and CLAUDE.md:35-36 tell consumers to load this config through `remote_config.url`. CodeRabbit documents that form as not recommended and offers `remote_config.repository`, which fits this repository's consumers because they share an owner.

## Evidence

README.md:9-10 and CLAUDE.md:35-36: `remote_config:` / `url: "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/coderabbit/refs/heads/main/coderabbit.yaml"`

docs.coderabbit.ai/getting-started/yaml-configuration, "External URL (not recommended)": "Shared configuration via URL is not recommended because it must be publicly reachable and is retrieved without authentication, which may expose sensitive configuration details."

Same page, Requirements: "A `url:` source must be publicly reachable over HTTPS. CodeRabbit retrieves it without authentication and the request times out after five seconds."

Same page, supported form: `remote_config:` with `repository:`, `ref:`, `path:`; "A bare `repository:` name resolves within the reviewed repository's owner or organization."

Validation: a file containing only the README's snippet fails schema.v2.json with "Additional properties are not allowed ('remote_config' was unexpected)". The schema has no `remote_config` property for either form, so this is a CodeRabbit docs-versus-schema gap that any consumer validating against the schema will hit.

## Impact

Every consumer depends on an unauthenticated fetch with a five-second limit. The documented sensitive-data concern does not apply here because this repository and file are public. The docs do not state what CodeRabbit does when the fetch fails.

## Fix

Change README.md:9-10 and CLAUDE.md:35-36 to the form below, and update consumer repositories. CodeRabbit must be able to access this repository.

```yaml
remote_config:
  repository: "coderabbit"
  ref: "main"
  path: "coderabbit.yaml"
```

Alternative: Central Configuration applies automatically to repositories with no config of their own, and this repository already has the required name. It requires renaming the file to `.coderabbit.yaml`, which breaks the current URL. The docs describe it for organizations and do not state whether a personal GitHub account qualifies.

## Resolution
README.md and CLAUDE.md now document remote_config.repository. Existing consumer repositories are outside this repository and still need their own update; the URL form keeps working while coderabbit.yaml stays at its path.
title: Documented consumption uses the remote_config URL form CodeRabbit marks not recommended

body:
## Problem

Class: config-drift. The config sets a key CodeRabbit has replaced. The published configuration reference no longer lists it, and the schema marks it deprecated and undocumented.

## Evidence

coderabbit.yaml:13: `request_changes_workflow: true`

schema.v2.json, `reviews.request_changes_workflow`: `"description": "Legacy alias for reviews.auto_approvals.enabled."`, `"deprecated": true`, `"x-undocumented": true`.

docs.coderabbit.ai/reference/configuration: zero occurrences of `request_changes_workflow`; `reviews.auto_approvals.enabled` is the documented key.

docs.coderabbit.ai/pr-reviews/automatic-approvals, "Legacy configuration key": "Use only one of the two keys. If a configuration sets both to different values, CodeRabbit turns off Automatic Approvals for that configuration and reports a configuration error."

## Impact

The alias works today. If CodeRabbit drops it, nothing fails: the `reviews` object has no `additionalProperties: false`, so schema validation still passes and approvals stop silently. A consumer that adds `auto_approvals.enabled` through inheritance with a different value triggers the documented configuration error.

## Fix

Replace line 13 with the documented key. Behavior is unchanged.

```yaml
  auto_approvals:
    enabled: true
```

## Resolution
Replaced reviews.request_changes_workflow with reviews.auto_approvals.enabled: true.
title: reviews.request_changes_workflow is a deprecated legacy alias

body:
## Problem

Class: dead config. The config sets `timeout_ms` on the GitHub Checks tool. The schema, the configuration reference, and the tool's own page define only `enabled`.

## Evidence

coderabbit.yaml:149: `timeout_ms: 90000`

schema.v2.json, `reviews.tools.github-checks`: `properties` contains only `enabled`.

docs.coderabbit.ai/reference/configuration: zero occurrences of `timeout_ms`.

docs.coderabbit.ai/tools/github-checks: `enabled` is the only documented option.

It passes validation because this object does not set `additionalProperties: false`; a planted unknown key at the same level also validated.

## Impact

The line reads as a 90-second wait that no CodeRabbit document says exists. A maintainer tuning check timing would edit it and see no documented effect.

## Fix

Delete line 149.

## Resolution
Removed timeout_ms with the github-checks block, whose remaining key equalled its default.
title: reviews.tools.github-checks.timeout_ms is not a documented setting

body:
## Problem

Class: missing-validation. CLAUDE.md:45 makes schema validation the pre-commit safeguard, but the official schema rejects unknown properties at the root and only 6 other objects. Stale or misspelled keys under `reviews`, including under `reviews.tools`, pass.

## Evidence

.pre-commit-config.yaml:21-29 runs `check-jsonschema` against schema.v2.json. CLAUDE.md:45: "Always validate against the official CodeRabbit schema before committing".

Probes with check-jsonschema 0.39.0 against the schema fetched 2026-11-10:
- unknown root key: fails, "Additional properties are not allowed"
- `reviews.not_a_real_key`: "ok -- validation done"
- `reviews.tools.github-checks.not_real`: "ok -- validation done"

In the schema, 111 object definitions with `properties` lack `additionalProperties: false` and 6 set it. The live instance is coderabbit.yaml:149, `timeout_ms`, which passes today.

## Impact

A green CI run does not show that every key is one CodeRabbit recognizes. A typo such as `auto_reviw:` under `reviews` passes and silently leaves the intended setting at its default across every consumer.

## Fix

Add this line under `## Validation Commands` in CLAUDE.md, using CodeRabbit's own command instead of a custom strict-schema tool:

"Schema validation does not reject unknown keys under `reviews`. After changing a key name, run `@coderabbitai configuration` on a pull request in a consuming repository and confirm the resolved YAML contains the setting."

## Resolution
Documented the schema limitation and the @coderabbitai configuration check in CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, as the finding specified. The upstream schema still accepts unknown keys under reviews.
title: Schema validation cannot detect unknown keys below the document root

body:
## Problem

The README describes `coderabbitai/ai-pr-reviewer` as the official repository, but that URL no longer resolves.

## Evidence

README.md:20: `- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/coderabbitai/ai-pr-reviewer) - Official AI PR Reviewer repository.`

An HTTP GET on that URL returned `404 Not Found`, and `gh api repos/coderabbitai/ai-pr-reviewer` returned `HTTP 404`.

## Impact

Readers following the link labeled official reach a missing page.

## Fix

Delete README.md:20. The Documentation link on README.md:19 covers the same need.

## Resolution
Removed the 404 link from README.md.
title: README links to a CodeRabbit repository that returns 404

body:
## Problem

Class: missing-project-license. The repository is public and tells readers how to consume the file, but it has no `LICENSE` file and GitHub reports no license.

## Evidence

`git ls-files` lists no LICENSE or COPYING file. `gh api repos/<owner>/coderabbit` returns `"license":null,"visibility":"public"`. README.md:4: "my base CodeRabbit configuration that I use in my other repositories."

Filed Low instead of the guide's High, which applies to a public repository intended for others to use: the README scopes use to the owner's own repositories.

## Impact

The owner is unaffected. Anyone else copying or referencing the configuration has no grant of rights.

## Fix

Add a `LICENSE` file with the owner's chosen SPDX license. If third-party reuse is not intended, say so in README.md.

## Resolution
Added an MIT LICENSE file, the owner's selection.
title: Public repository distributes coderabbit.yaml with no declared license
